questions.q: How does Conditional Split route rows by default (disjoint: false)?
options: Each row goes to only its first matching stream
Each row goes to every stream it matches
Rows are routed randomly among matching streams
Conditional Split can only have one output stream
questions.explain: With disjoint set to false (the common case), each row goes to the first condition it matches, not every condition it happens to satisfy.

questions.q: What does setting disjoint to true change?
options: A row can flow down every stream it matches, not just the first one
It disables the default stream entirely
It converts Conditional Split into a Join transformation
It has no effect on routing behavior
questions.explain: disjoint: true allows a single row to be routed to every matching stream simultaneously, rather than stopping at the first match.

questions.q: What does the Pivot transformation's "pivot key" control?
options: Which column's unique values become new columns in the output
Which columns are used to group rows before aggregating
The join condition between two streams
The row filter applied before pivoting
questions.explain: The pivot key is the column whose distinct row values each become a new output column, by default one column per unique value.

questions.q: What does Unpivot do, relative to Pivot?
options: The reverse — it collapses multiple columns into row-based name/value pairs
Exactly the same thing as Pivot, just with a different name
It deletes columns rather than reshaping them
It only works on numeric columns, unlike Pivot
questions.explain: Unpivot takes several columns and turns them into two: one holding the former column name, one holding that column's value — turning a wide table back into a long, tidy one.

questions.q: Why might a sink need Allow schema drift enabled when writing Pivot's output?
options: Pivoted column names are often generated dynamically at run time and may not appear in fixed metadata
Pivot never produces any real column names at all
Allow schema drift is required for every sink, regardless of the source transformation
Pivot output can never be written to a sink under any circumstances
questions.explain: Since pivoted columns can be created dynamically based on unique data values, schema drift on the sink lets those dynamically named columns land even when they aren't explicitly listed in metadata.
